transcript.text: Greenfield. GitHub repo github.com/BMA-Corgea/repo-tour exists but is EMPTY (no branches, description only). Product: take a repo, digest/understand it, and deliver a guided TOUR of it the same way the guided-tour skill tours an HTML UI (used for tutorials in GLP-Strong-App). Tour is played inside a GitHub-repo-page-lookalike UI. Side panel for notes, each note carrying metadata for WHICH TOUR STEP inspired it, so post-tour code review is better than LGTM. Chatbot during the tour answering questions, driven by Evan's Claude subscription. Must also work on PRs: explain before/after and WHY the change was made. Endgame: integrate into GONS so review can be deep when Evan wants to be involved in the code rather than dropped into a project cold.
Build repo-tour: agent-generated guided tours of a repo and of PRs, with provenance-tagged notes feeding deeper code review, eventually wired into GONS.

DECISIONS 2026-08-25: (1) Own pages, NOT a GitHub overlay. (2) SPEED IS NOT A PRIORITY — Evan: 'I'd rather get up and walk around for a few minutes while you enable me to understand a repo I would have had no hope of understanding before.' Cold-start latency is explicitly NOT a design constraint; thoroughness wins. (3) Deterministic/parser-based digestion is the preferred approach (tree-sitter etc. extracts structure; models interpret it). (4) REPO-FIRST for v1, not PR-first. (5) First real target is GUTS — he wants to visualize the GONS/GOMS work to see where it started and where it's going, instead of continually changing it without a sense of direction. (6) Wants a single-page HTML artifact visualizing the digest as part of the proposal.
